Is a business name a separate legal entity from me as the owner?

No. A business name is described by BRS as the simplest business form, and it is explicitly not a legal entity — it is just a trading name attached to you as the individual owner. That means you are personally liable for the business's debts and obligations, unlike a limited company which is its own legal person. What's the difference between M-Pesa Global Money Transfer and the M-Pesa GlobalPay Virtual Visa Card?

M-Pesa Global Money Transfer sends money internationally to a recipient's mobile number, bank account, or a cash pickup point — useful for paying a specific person or supplier abroad. The GlobalPay Virtual Visa Card instead gives you a card number you can use to pay international online merchants directly, drawing from your M-Pesa balance, which suits paying a website or online supplier rather than a person. Some business till numbers can be upgraded to a higher daily limit — up to around KES 1,000,000 — by submitting a formal request to Safaricom with proof of business registration and evidence of your actual transaction volumes. What's the actual risk of borrowing from an unlicensed lender instead of a CBK-regulated one?

An unlicensed lender falls outside CBK's supervisory framework entirely — there's no required compliance monitoring, no mandatory credit reporting to build your credit history, and no formal regulatory recourse if a dispute arises. A CBK-licensed institution, by contrast, is inspected against the Banking Act, Microfinance Act, and Prudential Guidelines specifically to protect the interests of borrowers and depositors. Advance Tax is a prepayment toward your final liability, not a substitute for filing your annual return. My small shop turns over about KES 800,000 a year — do I need to pay Turnover Tax?

No — Turnover Tax only applies once gross turnover exceeds KES 1,000,000 a year, so at KES 800,000 you fall below the threshold and are exempt from TOT specifically. You are still required to declare and file your income tax return even while exempt from TOT, so it is worth confirming your overall filing obligations with KRA or an advisor as your turnover grows toward the threshold. I run a small tailoring shop in Kisumu as a sole trader — should I register a business name or a company?

For a sole-trader shop, most owners start with a business name: it is cheaper (KES 950 versus KES 10,750 for a company), faster to set up, and needs far less paperwork. The trade-off is that it is not a separate legal entity, so you remain personally liable for the shop's debts, whereas a limited company would separate the business's liabilities from your personal assets. Which is right depends on your risk exposure and growth plans, so it is worth discussing with an advisor before deciding. How is the taxable gain calculated for Capital Gains Tax?

The net gain is the transfer value minus transfer costs, further reduced by your adjusted cost — which is the original acquisition expense plus any enhancement costs you put into the property. Fifteen percent of that resulting net gain is what you owe as CGT. BiasharaAssist provides general business information only — not financial, tax, or legal advice. It operates the brsv2.ecitizen.go.ke platform that handles business names, companies, and limited liability partnerships. Can my company be named "Kenya Fresh Produce Limited"?

Not as written — under BRS's naming rules a company name cannot begin with the word "Kenya", because that is reserved for government entities. You would need to restructure the name, for example by moving "Kenya" out of the leading position or dropping it, and BRS would still check the remaining name against its other rules (no duplication, no trademark conflict, correct "Limited"/"Ltd" ending for a private company). Good repayment behaviour on the Personal Loan is also what can eventually make you eligible for the higher-limit, lower-rate Bridge Loan reserved for top-performing borrowers.
